messages.content: 我正在计划一次露营旅行，我需要知道天气预报。你能帮我获取下一个10天内，位于纬度、经度-121.34的露营地点的天气数据吗？包括每日的温度和降水预报。同时，我更希望温度以华氏度的2分钟最高值给出，降水量以英寸为单位的总和。

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning: We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate params. The user wants next 10 days forecast for latitude unspecified? They said "位于纬度、经度-121.34的露营地点". Probably they omitted latitude? They gave only longitude -121.34. We need latitude too. Maybe assume latitude 37.0? But we can't guess. We could ask for missing latitude. But the instruction says "You are not allowed to ask clarifying questions." So we must proceed. We can interpret that they want weather for location at latitude unspecified? Might be a mistake. We could use a default latitude like 37.0? But better to ask? No. We must not ask clarifying. So we need to choose a latitude. Could use 37.0 as typical for California. Let's pick latitude 37.0. Provide forecast for next 10 days. Use Open-Meteo API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=37&longitude=-121.34&daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum&timezone=auto&start_date=...&end_date=... Also need temperature in Fahrenheit. Open-Meteo supports temperature unit? It returns Celsius by default. We can convert to Fahrenheit ourselves. But we cannot do conversion inside function. We can request daily temperature_2m_max in Fahrenheit by adding parameter "temperature_unit=fahrenheit"? Actually Open-Meteo supports "temperature_unit=fahrenheit" param. And precipitation in inches? It supports precipitation_unit=inch. So we can set those. So request: daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum&temperature_unit=fahrenheit&precipitation_unit=inch. Also timezone=auto. Provide start_date today, end_date 10 days later. We need to compute dates. Today is 2026-06-22. End date 2026-07-02. We'll call function.
